summary: Great Western Trail: Argentina reworks Pfister's cattle-driving engine around the Pampas, adding farmers and new route choices while keeping the deck-building and rondel core intact. It plays very similarly to the original but with fresh route decisions and a slightly different economic rhythm.
praised: fresh take on a proven engine-building formula
new farmer worker type adds decision variety
criticised: very similar bones to the original, so it can feel like more of the same to fans
still a long, dense game with real rules overhead
niche appeal to those who didn't like the original

interaction.kind: Same as Great Western Trail: building fees and contested track/delivery spaces, now alongside farmer paths
interaction.detail: Keeps GWT's structure of a mostly personal rondel/deck engine with shared trail buildings (paying opponents when you use theirs) and limited delivery/route spaces that players race for. The explicit solo mode suggests the core loop holds up without opponents, reinforcing that interaction is a secondary layer, not the main event.
interaction.said: unknown — spinoff hasn't accumulated the same volume of discussion as the original, though it's generally described in the same terms as base GWT

subsystems: Cattle drive & delivery to Buenos Aires
scoring.how_you_win: As in the original Great Western Trail, repeatedly herd cattle to the capital for delivery value while building up trail buildings and fields; highest total points when the end trigger fires wins.
